hero.title: Testable by design
intro.0: Some code fights every test you write; other code is a pleasure to check. The difference is not luck - it is design. Code that receives its dependencies, does one job, and hides no state is easy to test. And it turns out those exact habits are what the next part - the SOLID principles - make deliberate. Testing is where 'design for change' stops being an idea and starts being a feeling.
task.1.title: Inject so you can substitute
task.1.context: A class that builds its own dependency with `new` inside cannot be tested in isolation - you are stuck with the real thing. Make it substitutable: write a `Notifier` that receives an `IClock` through its constructor and uses it in `Ping()`. Now a test can hand in a fixed clock.
task.1.goal.0: Write a `Notifier` that takes an `IClock` in its constructor and has `Ping()` return `"early"` before noon, else `"late"`.
task.1.goal.1: Main hands in a fixed clock (9) and checks the result, so the output is PASS.
task.2.title: One job, one easy test
task.2.context: A class that computes, formats, and prints is hard to test - you cannot reach the answer without the rest running too. Give the calculation its own home. Write a `Scorer` with a `Score(int hits, int misses)` that returns `hits - misses` - one job, so a test can check it directly.
task.2.goal.0: Write a `Scorer` whose `Score(int hits, int misses)` returns `hits - misses`.
task.2.goal.1: Main checks `Score(5, 2)` is `3`, so the output is PASS.
task.3.title: No hidden state to trip on
task.3.context: The easiest code to trust takes its input and returns its output - nothing hidden, no surprises, the same answer every time. Write a `Prices` with a `Discount(int price, int percent)` that returns the reduced price. Given the same inputs, a test always gets the same result.
task.3.goal.0: Write a `Prices` whose `Discount(int price, int percent)` returns `price - price * percent / 100`.
task.3.goal.1: Main checks `Discount(100, 10)` is `90`, so the output is PASS.
task.4.title: Testable by design - recap
task.4.context: Code that is easy to test is code that is easy to change - the same habits underlie both.
task.4.summaryIntro: You do not bolt testability on afterwards. The shape that makes code easy to test is the shape that makes it easy to change.
task.4.summaryItems.0.title: Inject dependencies -
task.4.summaryItems.0.text: receive them, so a test can substitute a double. This is the **D** of SOLID, Dependency Inversion.
task.4.summaryItems.1.title: One job per class -
task.4.summaryItems.1.text: a single-purpose class has a single, simple test. This is the **S**, Single Responsibility.
task.4.summaryItems.2.title: No hidden state -
task.4.summaryItems.2.text: input in, output out is the easiest thing to trust.
task.4.summaryClose: These habits have names. Next: Design for change - the SOLID principles that make them deliberate.
concept.pr-testability.def: Shaping code so it is easy to check - injected dependencies, one job each, and no hidden state.
concept.pr-pure-function.def: Code that depends only on its inputs and keeps no hidden state, so the same call always gives the same result.
